title: Prove one interleaved g=31, q=26 word misses the endpoint.
body:
<!-- CURSOR_AGENT_PR_BODY_BEGIN -->
## Change and mathematical scope

Proof, for one call order and one legal frame. No new kappa.

On the paired-star contract, the full-call order that applies every first half in stage order and then every second half in the same order does not meet the endpoint at `g = 31`, `q = 26` for the legal frame `A = diag(I_q, 0)` and `B e_q = e_0` on every stage. The stage projectors do not commute. The pure product differs from `product_j (I + x_j E_j)` by the monomial `x_0 x_1` on an invariant plane. Thin maps do not change the pure factor, so no thin maps of any rank repair this order and frame.

The five rank-26 maps forced by setting every `D_j = 1` are explicit. They meet the normalized coefficient at that point and miss it at the two field points `(2, 4, 1, ..., 1)` and `(3, 5, 1, ..., 1)`. The same projectors meet the pure target when the halves of each stage stay adjacent. This is not the consecutive rank bound and not the adjacent-halves map count.

Selected κ stays `781451/250000000` from PR #6030. A failed search is not used as nonexistence. The result is this order and frame only.

## Task and overlap

Base commit `17469fff78c22941280f04d39dc5a1faee09c840` (canonical CrocSwap `main`). This fork draft uses `cursor/upstream-main-17469fff-b813` as its base because that branch is the same commit; the fork's own `main` is older. The upstream target is CrocSwap `main`.

Task card `joint-query-controller`, scope refined. The assigned question is the interleaved `g = 31`, `q = 26` profile left open by PR #7010. The first step was one pattern that separates stage halves, the thin maps forced by `D_j = 1`, and the normalized coefficient at two field points.

Nearest overlap:

- PR #7010 proves the adjacent-halves count, including the adjacent subcase of `g = 31`, `q = 26`. It names this interleaved profile as open and does not investigate it.
- PR #7005 proves the consecutive rank bound `R ≥ g q` and leaves internal-gap and other nested or crossing orders open. This package does not redo that bound and does not classify those schedules.
- PR #5747 is the contract, the rank floor, and the commuting map-count. The commuting count already excludes five maps when every full projector commutes. The frame here does not commute.

The `g = 3` censuses fix three leaves, block size 2, and entries in `F_2`. They are not a proof at thirty-one leaves or twenty-six ports.

## Validation

Python 3.12, no third-party packages.

```sh
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/paired-star-g31-q26-interleaved-five
```

Registered status: `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE` with outcome `negative-result`. Both the `python3 -I -B` replay and the `python3 -I -O -B` replay print `PASS_PAIRED_STAR_G31_Q26_INTERLEAVED`. Checks raise, so `-O` does not strip them.

The 6-by-6 difference is the exact product in `GF(2)[x_0, x_1]`. At both GF(16) points, all 36 entries of the `q = 26` pure product on that plane match the 6-by-6 product, and the normalized coefficient of the forced maps is not `I`. Setting the nonzero entry of `B` to zero makes the crossed pure product match. Deleting the five maps misses the `D_j = 1` point. A `q = 1` block engine agrees with `deriv · pure^{-1}`.

Not run: a proof assistant, a search over other orders or frames, a native or supplier replay, and `scripts/research_selected_baseline.py`. The selected record is provenance only.

## Credit

The paired-star contract, the rank floor, and the commuting map-count are from PR #5747 (Ali Romman), including PR #5673, PR #5631, and PR #5617. PR #7010 left this interleaved profile open. PR #7005 left internal-gap and other nested or crossing schedules open.

Prepared by unpaidmoon with substantial Cursor Grok assistance. Independent human review and a proof-assistant proof are unclaimed.

## Open next questions

- Does this same all-first-then-all-second order meet the endpoint for some other legal frame whose stage eigenbases are not the same? Form the two-stage cross product for one pair of legal frames that are not conjugate to the same `(A, B)`, and compare one off-diagonal block with the target before any native bill.
- A word that puts only thin maps between a stage's halves keeps the pure factor. That internal-gap schedule is the question left by PR #7005, not this order.

## Workflow feedback (optional)

The useful split was the pure factor from the normalized coefficient. At `D_j = 1` the crossed order looks successful, because every `x_j` vanishes. The mismatch appears only at a second field point, which is why that point was worth computing before any native bill.

Feedback discussion: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1200
